ads_ratio.reason: DATA_GAP:ads_ratio — VIV is a 20-F filer; engine per-share figures are per ordinary share while the traded NYSE price is per ADS. The ratio of 2 ordinary shares per ADS is stated in the filer's own FY2025 20-F (the ratio changed from 1 in the April 2025 transaction: 40-for-1 reverse split followed by a split under which 1 grouped share became 80 shares, a net doubling of the share count).
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed February 23, 2026), notes to the consolidated financial statements describing the 2025 reverse stock split / stock split transaction: '1 ADR now representing 2 ordinary shares issued by the Company, while the total number of ADRs in circulation remained unchanged.'

base_override.reason: SHARE_SCALE / BASE_DIVERGENCE: the engine's 3-yr median base ($2,068.56 per ADS in key_numbers.md) is a share-unit artefact. This run's financials_history.csv carries FY2023 1,658,604 and FY2024 1,643,132 as AdjustedWeightedAverageShares (filed in thousands, on the pre-April-2025 basis) beside FY2025 3,223,658,000 in units on the post-transaction basis. The OE legs are filed in BRL units, so only the denominator is wrong. Overrides fill missing periods only and cannot replace the filed FY2023/24 counts, and ttm.py cannot run on this IFRS filer (exit 3). The base is therefore pinned to the FY2025 figure the engine prints on the same weighted-average diluted count the CSV, the per-share history and the market cap use. Alternatives, quantified in analysis.md: the 2026-10-16 pin of 1.2803686126106435 divided the same FY2025 OE by the year-end cover-page count 3,195,606,352 (0.88% higher; replaced because it mixed a full-year flow with a year-end count); a 3-yr median on statements.json's restated FY2023/24 basic counts gives about $1.23 (lower); a TTM to 2026-06-30 from the 2Q26 ITR 6-K is outside bounded authority (c) and is escalated. All are Tier C on the engine's scenario math.
base_override.source: This run's dcf_numbers.json base_oe_latest_per_share 1.2692270927499132, copied verbatim (already per ADS; key_numbers.md 'Latest FY OE/share: $1.27'). It is the engine's FY2025 owner's earnings (base_oe_total_latest_fy 2,045,777,035.68, financials_history.csv oe_conservative FY2025) divided by the CSV's FY2025 shares_diluted 3,223,658,000 (the filing-sourced shares_override from the FY2025 20-F EPS note) and multiplied by the declared ads_ratio of 2. Kind 'estimate': the anchor is that engine-printed figure itself (ratio 1.0, inside the 0.1x-10x band).

moat_against: Claro (América Móvil) and TIM compete hard on price and network; prepaid switching costs are low
Capex intensity is structural (capex 16.4% of revenue in Q2 2026) — 5G and FTTH build never stops
Regulatory overhang: Anatel oversight and FISTEL TFF fees (the Q2 2026 release notes R$7.3B for 2020-2026 excluded from its debt figure)
BRL earnings priced in USD — real depreciation directly cuts per-ADS owner's earnings
Controlled company (Telefónica held 77.13% at Q1 2026) — minorities are subordinate to group strategy and a >=100%-of-net-income distribution commitment
moat_for: Largest Brazilian wireless carrier — about 33% market share with postpaid leadership (about 37% of postpaid)
Scale, spectrum holdings and the Vivo brand; record mobile ARPU in Q2 2026 prints
Extensive FTTH network enabling converged fixed-mobile cross-sell into its mobile base
Telefónica group parentage — technology, procurement and balance-sheet backing
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat: Brazil's largest wireless carrier (about 33% market share, postpaid leadership) with scale, spectrum, the Vivo brand and a large FTTH footprint enabling converged cross-sell, backed by the Telefónica group — against strong Claro/TIM competition, low prepaid switching costs, heavy 5G/FTTH capex intensity, Anatel regulation including the FISTEL fee overhang, BRL/USD exposure on a USD-priced ADS, and minority holders subordinate to the controlling parent.
name: TELEFONICA BRASIL S.A.
one_liner: Brazil's telecom incumbent, moat 5/10 — a 10.24% OE yield and +7.6% BRL revenue prints, but at $12.40 the weighted IRR is only 14.34% (bear 11.32%, bull 17.43%; IV@15% $11.72/ADS on a pinned FY2025 base of $1.27/ADS); it clears the 15% hurdle only at or below $11.72.
